classes_note: Four classes: (1) labor archives, the archives of labor and the left held for later readers (census kind, areas 'archives-and-custody' and 'movement-documents', evidence_kind 'archival collection'; B2, B4, B6, B8, and the snippets of B3 and B7); (2) archives held by a university, the university as holder (census operator and record.holder; B1, B4, B8); (3) custody of the record (census area 'archives-and-custody'; B1, B4, B8; the Capture Registry's finding 'THE CUSTODIAN OF THE UNIONS' OWN RECORDS'); (4) holding the losing side, membership sourced from the archive only (the census's organizing question, record.losing_side and ml_reading; the Capture Registry's finding that names #1725's question): the field states no losing side for the entity, so (4) is the archive's class for it and is marked so wherever it is used. Classes (3) and (4) were added after the first string pass and before the reading, on the reading of the hop candidates from #1725 (custody passages in #1066, #1634, #1679); the pass was rerun with all four. The census's urban-affairs, civil-rights and women's-workplace collecting (its record_object) is carried by the field and the record and enters no class pass of its own: the census gives it no area of its own. The aliases are the entity's names (the Walter P. Reuther Library; the Reuther Library; the Archives of Labor and Urban Affairs, and the Archives of Labor History and Urban Affairs, the form of the name in Pflug's 1974 guide as Wikipedia cites it; the Labor History Archives, its 1960 name) and its host (reuther.wayne.edu). 'Reuther' alone is not used: Walter Reuther, the UAW president for whom the library is named, is a person distinct from the entity, and Victor Reuther another. Wayne State University (the holder and operator) and the UAW (the funder of its building and the union whose records it keeps) are entities distinct from the library and are not aliases. The census's ml_reading applies #1725's question (whose record, who holds it, whether the losing side is kept) to the entity: that reading is the archive's, ledgered as ML-NN. #1725 (Ils ne sont pas marxistes, AXN:0B50), the census's anchor, is read at the passages that name the entity's kind: the holder, the organ, the losing position and the record of a split. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it; R where it states a relation between the entity and an archive object; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category (the holder, the organ, the losing position, custody of the record, the archive's own account of archives and their holders) to one of the two classes; a bare mention, a citation line or a list of keywords is not a claim.
